'''Liu Ruozhuang''' ({{zh|s=刘若庄}}; 25 May 1925 - 8 October 2020) was a Chinese physical chemist and academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS).<ref name="tiger">{{cite news |date=9 October 2020 |editor1=Liu Jiani ({{lang|zh|刘佳妮}}) |title= |script-title=zh:著名物理化学家、中科院院士刘若庄去世，享年95岁 |url=http://www.bjnews.com.cn/news/2020/10/09/775769.html |accessdate=18 October 2020 |work=[[Beijing News]] |language=zh}}</ref> He was the founder of computational chemistry in China.<ref name="fly">{{cite news |author1=Jiang Ziwen ({{lang|zh|蒋子文}}) |date=9 October 2020 |title= |script-title=zh:中国计算化学奠基人、中科院院士刘若庄逝世，享年95岁 |url=https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_9491084 |accessdate=18 October 2020 |work=[[The Paper (newspaper)|The Paper]] |language=zh}}</ref>

==Biography==
Liu was born in [[Beijing]], on May 25, 1925. In 1943, he entered [[Fu Jen Catholic University]], majoring in chemistry at the Department of Chemistry. After graduating in 1947, he did his postgraduate work at [[Peking University]]. In 1949, he published his first research paper "Modified Troutons Rule" in the ''Journal of the Chinese Chemical Society''. In June 1950, he began to study quantum chemistry under the supervision of Tang Aoqing. In September 1951, he was hired as a lecturer at [[Peking University]] and Fu Jen Catholic University. In 1952, after the adjustment of colleges and departments, he taught at [[Beijing Normal University]], where he was promoted to associate professor in September 1956 and to full professor in July 1979. He joined the [[Jiusan Society]] in 1956.{{cn|date=June 2024}} In 1978, he founded the Laboratory of Quantum Chemistry at Beijing Normal University. He joined the [[Chinese Communist Party]] in 1984.{{cn|date=June 2024}} He became a visiting professor at the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] in the following year. He died in Beijing, on October 8, 2020.<ref name="fly"/>
